Tanzania · Contact

Request a proposal for a survey in Tanzania

Tell us about the wayleave, reserve, licence area or project site, and what the record is for. We reply by email with the questions we need answered, and then with a written proposal covering the scope, the imagery plan and its dates, the method, the deliverables and the schedule.

About you
About the route or site

What do you need?

Location or province, the buffer distances to check, and any date the record must reflect.

Your request reaches us through FormSubmit, a form-delivery service. Read the privacy notice.

What happens next

  1. We reply by email to confirm what we need from you.
  2. A short scoping call about the route or site, the distances that matter and the imagery.
  3. A written proposal: scope, imagery plan, method, deliverables and schedule.

What to send

The route or boundary file (KML, KMZ, GeoJSON, Shapefile, GPX or GeoPackage), the country and province, the distances to check, the date the record must reflect, the deliverables you need and your deadline. No file yet? Describe the location and we can draw the route with you.

Procurement teams

Send your supplier or prequalification forms, or the tender documents, with your request. The proposal states which registrations are in place for your contract and which are being arranged.

For a wayleave, reserve or site in Tanzania

  • Region and district, so we can check the imagery that exists for the area.
  • The widths to report: the wayleave in your own acquisition or agreement, the road reserve for the road class, the 30 m railway reserve, a safety zone, or your company standard. Up to six widths in one survey.
  • Any valuation or cut-off date, and any notice already issued, so the imagery plan can match those dates.
  • Satellite only, or drone detail too. Drone work in Tanzania needs an operator with a Tanzanian ROC, a security clearance and TCAA’s authorisation for each operation, so the proposal shows the lead time. See drone law in Tanzania.
  • What the register is for: maintenance, a wayleave or reserve dispute, a new route, a resettlement baseline or lenders’ monitoring.
  • Oil, gas or mining work: tell us, because the proposal then sets out its local-content position under the Petroleum Act or the Mining (Local Content) Regulations.

Frequently asked questions

Do you need a site visit or a drone flight to start?

No. A survey starts from your route or boundary file and dated satellite imagery, open building datasets or the imagery you already hold, so nobody travels and no aircraft flies. Drone detail is added only where a stretch needs it, subject to the TCAA approvals and security clearances each job requires.

Our own teams already fly drones. Can you use that imagery?

Yes, if it was flown under the approvals GN 268 of 2026 requires. Say which stretches the orthophotos cover and when they were captured; we test a sample for resolution and quality first, and agree how the files reach us, because this form carries your request only.

We only have a wayleave drawing or a list of beacons. Is that enough?

Yes. Send the drawing, the tower or kilometre-post coordinates, or the road or railway section with its start and end points, and we digitise the centre line and the reserve with you. You confirm it before any survey runs, so every distance in the register is measured from a line you have agreed.

Our tender runs on NeST. Can you respond there?

Name the tender number and the procuring entity in your request, and attach any prequalification or vendor forms. Our notes for procurement teams set out what the Public Procurement Act, 2023 and the local-content rules mean for this kind of service.
